headline: Indiana eats like a Friday-night gym: tenderloins wider than the bun, sugar cream pie.
summary: Indiana's food is proud, plain and oversized, from the breaded pork tenderloin that hangs off its bun to sugar cream pie and gym-concession popcorn. Game nights run through century-old downtown institutions a short walk from Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Newer Indy cooks in Fletcher Place and two immigrant corridors. This is written from model knowledge, so scout the arena vendors and newer spots before anyone acts.

insights.title: The tenderloin is judged by its overhang
insights.detail: Indiana's signature sandwich is a pork loin pounded thin, breaded, fried and served far wider than its bun. Nick's Kitchen in Huntington claims the 1908 original. In Indy the classic carriers are drive-ins and taverns like Mug-n-Bun in Speedway (1960, carhops and house root beer) and Plump's Last Shot in Broad Ripple. The Indiana Foodways Alliance maps a statewide tenderloin trail.
insights.implication: "Bigger than the bun" is a graphic idea locals already love: a shape that breaks its own frame. Run it as a playful overhang motif on caps and tees. Make it a paid, licensed collab with a named drive-in, not generic food clip art.

insights.title: St. Elmo's shrimp cocktail is downtown's power ritual
insights.detail: St. Elmo Steak House has served steaks a few blocks from the Fieldhouse since 1902. Its shrimp cocktail comes buried in a horseradish-heavy sauce that clears the sinuses. Every first-timer gets dared to eat it, and the sauce sells in jars in Indiana grocery stores. The Huse family's restaurant is the big-night table for Pacers, Colts and Indy 500 crowds.
insights.implication: Cocktail red and horseradish cream make an insider colorway story any Hoosier will recognize. Using the St. Elmo name, its 1902 mark or the jar label needs a license and a paid partnership.

insights.title: Hoosier Hysteria has a concession stand
insights.detail: Statewide basketball religion is lived in small-town gyms like New Castle Fieldhouse (the largest high school gym in the world) and the Hoosier Gym in Knightstown. There, the popcorn machine and a menu board of tenderloins and pie are part of the ritual. Indiana is one of the nation's top popcorn producers, and Orville Redenbacher was a Hoosier. In Broad Ripple, Bobby Plump, whose shot won Milan's 1954 state title, lent his name to Plump's Last Shot, a restaurant full of that history.
insights.implication: A gym-concessions capsule (popcorn stripes, menu-board type, a "Last Shot" story) ties the Pacers to the statewide high school game, not just downtown. Time it to the IHSAA state finals, played at Gainbridge in March.

insights.title: Sugar cream pie is a humble state treasure
insights.detail: Sugar cream pie, Indiana's official state pie since 2009, came out of east-central Indiana's Shaker and Amish kitchens. It's a "desperation pie," made from pantry staples when the fruit ran out: cream, sugar and a dusting of nutmeg. Wick's Pies in Winchester has made it at scale since the 1940s.
insights.implication: A custard-cream base with a nutmeg-speckle texture makes a warm winter colorway. It sits naturally beside the white, royal blue and gold of the returning Moments Mixtape City Edition. Nobody owns the pie, so the palette is free to use. Wick's branding is not.

insights.title: The new food city: Lafayette Road and the Southside
insights.detail: The International Marketplace on the northwest side packs Mexican, West African, Vietnamese, Middle Eastern and South Asian restaurants and grocers along Lafayette Road. The Southside (Perry Township toward Southport and Greenwood) is home to the largest Chin refugee community in the U.S. Its restaurants serve dishes like sabuti, a hominy-corn soup.
insights.implication: These neighborhoods hold many of Indy's newer fans and rarely show up in Pacers product. Commission anything here through the International Marketplace Coalition and Chin community organizations, and credit and pay local artists. Never mash the cultures into a generic "world food" graphic.

insights.title: Fletcher Place chefs and a feeding mission
insights.detail: Jonathan Brooks's Milktooth (he was a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2016) and Bluebeard, named for the Kurt Vonnegut novel, made Fletcher Place the city's chef-driven strip. Milktooth briefly closed in early 2026 for an Arlene's conversion and is reportedly returning. Martha Hoover's Patachou group runs Public Greens, whose profits help fund the Patachou Foundation's meals for food-insecure kids.
insights.implication: Hoover's foundation is a credible community-investment partner for a Cup-week or holiday giving night. Fletcher Place is a design-forward setting for a launch dinner. Confirm both restaurants are still operating first.

insights.title: 2026-27 gives the food map a basketball calendar
insights.detail: Haliburton returns in a season when Indiana hosts the 76ers and new Sixer LeBron James on the Oct 30 Cup Night. The Dec 11 NBA Cup final comes to Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse. Fans will fill the Fieldhouse corridor (St. Elmo, the Slippery Noodle, Bicentennial Unity Plaza) and the old College Avenue taverns near Hinkle, like the Red Key.
insights.implication: Build a "Gainbridge to Hinkle" Cup-week food-map capsule that works whether or not the Pacers reach the final. Keep it team- and city-led, because Haliburton's signature footwear sits with another brand, not Nike.

places.name: St. Elmo Steak House
places.why: The 1902 steakhouse a few blocks from Gainbridge. Its horseradish shrimp cocktail is Indy's best-known dish, and its dining room is the pre-game power table.

places.name: Slippery Noodle Inn
places.neighborhood: Downtown (South Meridian St, near Union Station)
places.why: Indiana's oldest bar (1850) has live blues and sits just south of the Fieldhouse, a walkable stop before or after the game.

places.name: Bicentennial Unity Plaza
places.why: The Fieldhouse's outdoor plaza hosts Pacers watch parties and winter skating. It's the natural home for food-truck and product pop-ups.

places.name: Shapiro's Delicatessen
places.why: A cafeteria-line Jewish deli since 1905. Corned beef and cheesecake before a game is a long-running Indy habit.

places.name: Long's Bakery
places.why: Cash-only glazed yeast doughnuts since 1955. The line out the door and the plain white box are pure Indy.

places.name: Mug-n-Bun
places.why: A 1960 carhop drive-in near the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, known for tenderloins, house root beer in frosted mugs and its retro sign.

places.name: Plump's Last Shot
places.why: Named for Bobby Plump's 1954 Milan game-winner, it's where tenderloins meet Hoosier Hysteria memorabilia.

places.name: Red Key Tavern
places.why: A post-Prohibition neighborhood tavern a short drive from Hinkle Fieldhouse, and the old-Indy hangout for Cup-final week.

places.name: International Marketplace
places.neighborhood: Northwest side (Lafayette Rd and W 38th St)
places.why: Indy's densest immigrant food corridor, with Mexican, West African, Asian and Middle Eastern restaurants and grocers.

places.name: Southside Chin corridor
places.why: Restaurants and groceries serving the largest Chin community in the U.S.

people.name: Bobby Plump
people.role: Milan High's 1954 state-title hero and namesake of Plump's Last Shot
people.why: He's the direct link between Hoosier Hysteria lore and an Indy dining room. Any "Last Shot" story should go through him and the family restaurant.

people.name: Craig Huse
people.role: Owner of Huse Culinary (St. Elmo Steak House, Harry & Izzy's)
people.why: Steward of Indy's most famous restaurant brand and its grocery-shelf cocktail sauce, and the licensing door for any St. Elmo collab.

people.name: Martha Hoover
people.role: Founder of Patachou Inc. and the Patachou Foundation
people.why: Indy's most prominent restaurateur-activist. Her foundation feeds food-insecure kids, which makes it a ready community partner.

people.name: Jonathan Brooks
people.why: The 2016 Food & Wine Best New Chef put Indy on the national food map, and he's a design-minded chef voice.

people.name: Brian Shapiro
people.why: Keeps a 1905 deli that carries Indy's Jewish heritage on South Meridian, a short walk from the Fieldhouse.

people.name: Indiana Foodways Alliance
people.role: Nonprofit that maps Indiana's culinary trails
people.why: Keeper of the statewide tenderloin and pie trails, and a credible partner for deciding which tenderloin counts.

people.name: International Marketplace Coalition
people.role: Community development nonprofit for the Lafayette Road corridor
people.why: The right partner for commissioning immigrant-owned businesses and artists, with the community credited and paid.

people.name: Wick's Pies
people.role: Sugar cream pie maker in Winchester, Indiana
people.why: The best-known commercial sugar cream pie in the state, and licensable for a Hoosier-pie hangtag or launch giveaway.

moments.name: Pre-game on the Fieldhouse corridor
moments.why: St. Elmo, the Slippery Noodle and Shapiro's, all within walking distance, are where Pacers nights start.

moments.name: Emirates NBA Cup championship at Hinkle Fieldhouse
moments.why: A national basketball audience comes to Butler-Tarkington, so the College Avenue taverns and downtown restaurants become the Cup-week food map.

moments.name: Devour Indy (winter edition)
moments.why: The citywide prix-fixe restaurant weeks land mid-season, a natural window for a food-themed drop.

moments.name: Chin National Day
moments.why: Indy's Chin community celebrates its national day with food and traditional dress. Engage only by invitation and partnership.

moments.name: IHSAA boys basketball state finals
moments.why: Small-town Indiana brings its own concession-stand culture into the Pacers' arena. This is the moment for a Hoosier Hysteria capsule.

moments.name: Indianapolis 500 milk toast
moments.why: Every Hoosier knows the winner drinks milk, but the marks and imagery belong to the Speedway.

moments.name: Indiana State Fair
moments.why: Pork-tent tenderloins, Dairy Barn milkshakes and elephant ears make it the state's biggest food gathering, right in the NBA offseason.

moments.name: Mitchell Persimmon Festival
moments.why: Southern Indiana's persimmon-pudding contest marks the run-up to tip-off.

vocabulary.meaning: In Indiana this means the breaded pork tenderloin sandwich, not the cut of meat.
The standard test and praise for a tenderloin: the wider the overhang, the better.
The official state pie, also called "desperation pie" because it's made from pantry staples.
An affectionate nickname for Indianapolis, common on local tees and among Pacers fans.
Shorthand for the Slippery Noodle Inn, the downtown blues bar.
A Chin hominy-corn soup found on Southside Chin restaurant menus.
Brown County's signature side, served at Nashville, Indiana restaurants and copied across the state.
Southern Indiana's fall dessert, made from wild native persimmons.

designCues.source: St. Elmo's shrimp cocktail sauce, the dish every Indy first-timer is dared to eat.
designCues.use: A heat accent (jock tag, waistband taping, lining) against Pacers navy #002D62. Name it for the dish, not for St. Elmo, unless the collab is licensed.
A base for a winter lifestyle colorway with Pacers gold #FDBB30 hits. It sits beside the white, royal blue and gold Moments Mixtape City Edition without clashing.

designCues.source: The browned, nutmeg-dusted top of a sugar cream pie.
designCues.use: A fine brown (#7A4A26) speckle on cream midsoles, fleece or a printed lining.

designCues.source: The breaded tenderloin hanging past its bun, Indiana's sandwich test.
designCues.use: Graphics and patches that deliberately overhang their frame or a cap crown. Use a toasted crumb gold (#C98B2E) that reads apart from Pacers gold.

designCues.source: Mug-n-Bun's carhop drive-in sign and the changeable plastic letters on Indiana high school concession boards.
designCues.use: Custom script and block letterforms for "Naptown" and "Tenderloin / Sugar Cream / Popcorn" menu graphics. Draw new type instead of copying any business's sign.

designCues.source: Small-town gym concession popcorn from one of America's top popcorn states.
designCues.use: A navy-and-gold vertical stripe in popcorn-box proportions, on shorts side panels or packaging for the state-finals capsule.

designCues.source: Bobby Plump's 1954 Milan game-winner, kept alive in the Broad Ripple restaurant that bears his name.
designCues.use: A hangtag and packaging story linking Indy's dinner tables to Hoosier Hysteria. Tell it with Plump's participation and paid credit, using the real history rather than the "Hoosiers" film.

productHooks: "Bigger Than the Bun" cap and tee: a toasted-gold, tenderloin-shaped Pacers patch that overhangs the crown. Launch it with a paid pop-up at a named tenderloin institution (Mug-n-Bun or Plump's Last Shot), and add stops on the Indiana Foodways Alliance trail.
"Sugar Cream" winter colorway: custard-cream fleece and a lifestyle shoe with a nutmeg-speckle midsole and navy/gold hits. Release it during Devour Indy, with a licensed Wick's pie in the launch box.
"Concession Stand" capsule for IHSAA state finals week at Gainbridge: popcorn-stripe shorts, menu-board graphic tees and a "Last Shot" story tee made with Plump's Last Shot.

"Gainbridge to Hinkle" Cup-week food-map tee and tote for the Dec 11 NBA Cup final. It plots St. Elmo, the Slippery Noodle, Shapiro's, Long's and the Red Key, with each named business licensed and paid.
"Horseradish Heat" shooting shirt in cocktail red and horseradish cream, for a marquee late-season home game. Make it a licensed St. Elmo collab with a jar-label hangtag.

Lafayette Road and Southside artist series: limited Pacers graphic tees commissioned from immigrant-community artists through the International Marketplace Coalition and Chin community groups, with proceeds shared.
watchouts: Every named business (St. Elmo, Mug-n-Bun, Long's, Wick's, Plump's Last Shot) holds its own marks. Use dish names and new artwork unless a collab is licensed and paid. The Speedway owns the Indy 500 and its milk-ritual imagery, and MGM owns the "Hoosiers" film.
Haliburton's signature footwear is with Puma (verify). Keep food-themed footwear and stories team- and city-led, not built around him.
Taverns and blues bars anchor game nights. Keep alcohol brands (Sun King, bar marks) off youth sizes and within NBA alcohol-marketing rules.

Indianapolis's Chin community came as refugees from persecution in Myanmar. Don't use Chin textiles or national symbols, and don't turn immigrant food into "exotic" graphics. Work through community organizations, and credit and pay the people involved.
The tenderloin joke is local pride, not a weight joke, so avoid overeating or "fat Midwest" caricature. Don't make pork the only food story either, since not every fan eats it.
